confusion_boundaries: An attached object needs a visible skin carrier and contact relation; a star in the background, bokeh, hair ornament or pendant is not applied cheek makeup.
Thin shaped glitter differs from a faceted crystal and from an irregular metallic foil patch. Reflective appearance alone does not prove a piece is made of actual metal.
Cosmetic paint belongs to a surface layer, not natural pigmentation, a scar, freckles, diagnosed skin condition or injected tattoo ink. Appearance cannot prove removal history or product formulation.
A connected openwork adhesive panel must expose facial skin through its gaps; textile lace belonging to a garment is a different carrier.
Body and hand additions require explicit cosmetic context and the selected skin region; they do not authorize changing clothing, pose, crop, actor count or age.
The FDA decal source supports carrier taxonomy only; its temporary tattoo label is not adopted as slot eligibility.
All authored records remain discovery-only; no semantic proof or native approval is asserted.
recommendations: Integrate only reviewed distinct meanings; retain existing generic gems, foil, faux freckles and decals without synonym additions.
Repeat the identical baseline query under the same sealed whole-pool H-F2 search and report source recall separately from native eligibility.
Use additional carrier/medium probes to detect whether gains generalize beyond the known cheek decoration request.
If existing useful records remain buried after additions, report residual exposure; do not change the user query or fabricate rank metadata.
